title: Deuteronomy Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 16.

questions.question: In which month does the LORD command to observe the Passover?
options: Month of Abib
Month of Tishri
Month of Nisan
Month of Elul
questions.correctAnswer: Month of Abib
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:1 commands to observe the month of Abib for the Passover.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 16, what kind of bread must be eaten for seven days during Passover?
options: Leavened bread
Unleavened bread
Barley bread
Rye bread
questions.correctAnswer: Unleavened bread
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:3 states that seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread during the Passover.

questions.question: True or False: The Passover sacrifice must be offered within any of the gates given by the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:5 says thou mayest not sacrifice the Passover within any of thy gates.

questions.question: Where does the LORD choose for the sacrifice of the Passover to be made?
options: In the place the LORD shall choose to place his name
In the city gates
In every household
In the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: In the place the LORD shall choose to place his name
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:2 and 16:6 specify that the Passover sacrifice is to be made in the place the LORD shall choose to place his name.

questions.question: True or False: No leavened bread shall be seen with you in all your coast for seven days during Passover.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:4 commands that no leavened bread shall be seen with thee for seven days.

questions.question: When shall the Passover sacrifice be offered?
options: At the going down of the sun
At dawn
At noon
At midnight
questions.correctAnswer: At the going down of the sun
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:6 states the Passover sacrifice shall be offered at even, at the going down of the sun.

questions.question: What must happen to the Passover sacrifice meat on the first day at even according to Deuteronomy 16?
options: None of it shall remain until the morning
It must be eaten raw
It can be stored overnight
It must be given to the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: None of it shall remain until the morning
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:4 commands that no flesh of the Passover sacrifice shall remain all night until the morning.

questions.question: How many days shall you eat unleavened bread during the Passover feast?
options: Seven days
Six days
Five days
Four days
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:3 instructs to eat unleavened bread for seven days during Passover.

questions.question: What is the bread of affliction meant to remind you of?
options: That you came out of Egypt in haste
That you are free from sin
That you shall not work on the Sabbath
That you must give offerings
questions.correctAnswer: That you came out of Egypt in haste
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:3 calls the unleavened bread the bread of affliction because you came out of Egypt in haste.

questions.question: True or False: After roasting and eating the Passover sacrifice, you shall remain at the place and not return to your tents.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:7 commands that after eating, you shall turn in the morning and go unto your tents.

questions.question: On which day shall there be a solemn assembly and no work done during the Passover feast?
options: Seventh day
First day
Third day
Fifth day
questions.correctAnswer: Seventh day
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:8 states that on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly with no work done.

questions.question: What is the duration of eating unleavened bread as commanded in Deuteronomy 16:8?
options: Six days
Seven days
Five days
Four days
questions.correctAnswer: Six days
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:8 says six days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, then the seventh is a solemn assembly.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 16 commands to observe the Passover because the LORD brought you out of Egypt by day.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:1 specifies the LORD brought thee out of Egypt by night, not by day.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 16, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Keep the Passover in the month of Abib
Do not work on the seventh day
Sacrifice the Passover at the place the LORD chooses
Eat unleavened bread for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the Passover in the month of Abib
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:1 is the first instruction commanding to observe the month of Abib and keep the Passover.

questions.question: Where must the Passover sacrifice be roasted and eaten?
options: In the place which the LORD thy God shall choose
In the city gates
In the fields
In the houses
questions.correctAnswer: In the place which the LORD thy God shall choose
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:7 states that the Passover sacrifice must be roasted and eaten in the place the LORD chooses.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 16:9, when should the seven weeks be counted?
options: From the time the sickle is first put to the corn
From the beginning of the new year
From the last day of the feast of unleavened bread
From the day of the first full moon
questions.correctAnswer: From the time the sickle is first put to the corn
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:9 instructs to number seven weeks beginning from the time the sickle is first put to the corn. This sets the timing for the Feast of Weeks as explained in verses 9-10.

questions.question: What kind of offering does Deuteronomy 16:10 say should be given at the feast of weeks?
options: A tribute of a freewill offering of thine hand
A sacrifice of the firstborn
A tithe of all produce
A burnt offering of lambs
questions.correctAnswer: A tribute of a freewill offering of thine hand
questions.explanation: Verse 10 specifies that the feast of weeks is to be kept with a freewill offering given to the LORD according to how He has blessed each person, highlighting generosity and gratitude.

questions.question: Who are included in the joyful celebration before the LORD in Deuteronomy 16:11?
options: Thou, thy family, servants, Levites, strangers, fatherless, and widows
Only the priests and Levites
The elders of the city and their families
All men of Israel above twenty years old
questions.correctAnswer: Thou, thy family, servants, Levites, strangers, fatherless, and widows
questions.explanation: Verse 11 emphasizes inclusive joy before the LORD involving family, servants, Levites, and vulnerable members of society, teaching communal rejoicing and hospitality.

questions.question: What reason does Deuteronomy 16:12 give for observing the statutes and remembering the feast?
options: Because you were a bondman in Egypt
Because of the promised land's abundance
Because of the presence of the Levites
Because the priests commanded it
questions.correctAnswer: Because you were a bondman in Egypt
questions.explanation: Verse 12 commands remembering the past bondage in Egypt as motivation to observe God's statutes, encouraging gratitude and faithfulness.

questions.question: How long is the feast of tabernacles to be observed according to Deuteronomy 16:13?
options: Seven days after gathering in the corn and wine
Three days during the new moon
One day of solemn assembly
Four weeks starting from the harvest
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days after gathering in the corn and wine
questions.explanation: Verse 13 specifies a seven-day observance of the feast of tabernacles following the harvest, linking worship with thanksgiving for provision.

questions.question: Who, besides the family, is included in the rejoicing during the feast of tabernacles as per Deuteronomy 16:14?
options: Manservant, maidservant, Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow
Only the priests and Levites
Only the elders of the tribe
All male Israelites over 20
questions.correctAnswer: Manservant, maidservant, Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow
questions.explanation: Verse 14 repeats the inclusive nature of the feast by naming servants, Levites, strangers, fatherless, and widows, promoting community fellowship and care.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Deuteronomy 16:15 for keeping the solemn feast unto the LORD?
options: Because the LORD will bless thee in all thine increase and works
Because it is commanded in the law of Moses
Because the priests require it
Because the land must be rested
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD will bless thee in all thine increase and works
questions.explanation: Verse 15 connects the feast with joy due to the LORD's blessings on increase and work, teaching gratitude and trust in God's provision.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 16:16, how many times in a year must all males appear before the LORD, and at which feasts?
options: Three times; at the feast of unleavened bread, feast of weeks, and feast of tabernacles
Once; at the feast of tabernacles only
Twice; at the feast of unleavened bread and feast of weeks
Four times; including the new moon celebrations
questions.correctAnswer: Three times; at the feast of unleavened bread, feast of weeks, and feast of tabernacles
questions.explanation: Verse 16 instructs males to appear before the LORD thrice yearly at these specific feasts, emphasizing obedience and communal worship.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 16:17 teach about giving during the feasts?
options: Every man shall give as he is able according to the LORD's blessing
Everyone must give the same fixed amount
Only the wealthy should give offerings
Giving is optional and has no set measure
questions.correctAnswer: Every man shall give as he is able according to the LORD's blessing
questions.explanation: Verse 17 promotes generosity proportional to one's ability and blessings, encouraging sincere and willing giving.

questions.question: Based on Deuteronomy 16:18, what qualities must judges and officers have in their judgment?
options: They must judge the people with just judgment
They may favor the rich if it benefits the city
They should listen only to the elders
They can accept gifts to influence decisions
questions.correctAnswer: They must judge the people with just judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 18 commands just judgment by appointed judges and officers, teaching integrity and fairness in leadership.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 16:19 warn against in judicial matters?
options: Not to wrest judgment, respect persons, or take a gift
To always trust the wealthy's testimony
To judge quickly without hearing both sides
To favor those who bring offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Not to wrest judgment, respect persons, or take a gift
questions.explanation: Verse 19 forbids perverting justice by partiality or bribery, emphasizing impartiality and righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 16:20 teaches that following what is altogether just leads to life and inheritance of the land.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states that pursuing complete justice results in life and possession of the land God gives, highlighting the blessing of obedience.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 16:21 prohibit planting near the altar of the LORD?
options: A grove of any trees
Vines or fruit trees
Grain crops
Flowers and herbs
questions.correctAnswer: A grove of any trees
questions.explanation: Verse 21 forbids planting groves near the altar to prevent idolatrous practices, teaching purity in worship.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 16:22, setting up an image is acceptable if it honors the LORD thy God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 22 declares that setting up any image is hated by the LORD, regardless of intent, forbidding idolatry.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 16:11 suggest about how rejoicing before the LORD should impact social relationships?
options: It includes joy shared with family, servants, Levites, strangers, fatherless, and widows
It should be a private celebration with only family
It excludes non-Israelites and servants
It requires separate celebrations for different groups
questions.correctAnswer: It includes joy shared with family, servants, Levites, strangers, fatherless, and widows
questions.explanation: Verse 11 teaches that rejoicing before the LORD is communal and inclusive, fostering unity and compassion within the community.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 16.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 16, how often must all the males appear before the LORD in the place He chooses?
options: Once a year
Twice a year
Three times a year
Four times a year
questions.correctAnswer: Three times a year
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:16 commands that all males shall appear three times in a year before the LORD in the place He chooses, specifically during the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks, and the feast of tabernacles.

questions.question: What is the primary qualification for the amount each man shall give according to Deuteronomy 16?
options: A fixed portion for all
Based on the size of his family
As he is able, according to the blessing God has given
Equal shares for all
questions.correctAnswer: As he is able, according to the blessing God has given
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:17 states that every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the LORD God which He has given him, emphasizing voluntary and proportionate giving.

questions.question: What is the role of judges and officers as commanded in Deuteronomy 16:18?
options: To collect taxes from the people
To lead the people in battle
To judge the people with just judgment throughout the tribes
To perform sacrifices at the altar
questions.correctAnswer: To judge the people with just judgment throughout the tribes
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:18 commands that judges and officers be appointed in all gates throughout the tribes to judge the people with just judgment, ensuring fair and righteous governance.

questions.question: What warning does Deuteronomy 16:19 give regarding judgment?
options: Judges should respect wealthy persons
It is permissible to accept gifts if the person is righteous
Judges must not wrest judgment, respect persons, or accept gifts
Judges should always favor their kin
questions.correctAnswer: Judges must not wrest judgment, respect persons, or accept gifts
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:19 warns judges not to distort justice, show partiality, or accept bribes, as gifts blind the eyes of the wise and pervert the words of the righteous.

questions.question: What is the ultimate goal of following just judgment according to Deuteronomy 16:20?
options: To gain wealth and power
That you may live and inherit the land the LORD gives
To be respected by the people
To avoid punishment
questions.correctAnswer: That you may live and inherit the land the LORD gives
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:20 teaches that following justice is essential for life and inheriting the land given by the LORD, linking righteousness with covenant blessings.

questions.question: Which of the following is forbidden near the altar of the LORD according to Deuteronomy 16:21?
options: Planting a grove of trees
Building a well
Setting up a tent
Lighting a fire
questions.correctAnswer: Planting a grove of trees
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:21 explicitly forbids planting a grove of any trees near the altar of the LORD, reflecting a prohibition against idolatrous practices connected to sacred groves in the ancient Near East.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 16:22 command regarding images?
options: Set up images to honor the LORD
Set up any image except at the altar
Do not set up any images because the LORD hates them
Only set up images of angels
questions.correctAnswer: Do not set up any images because the LORD hates them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:22 forbids setting up any image because the LORD hates them, emphasizing the monotheistic purity and prohibition of idolatry in Israel’s worship.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the command in Deuteronomy 16:19 to avoid bribery and partiality in judgment?
options: Exodus 23:8
Genesis 1:1
Psalms 23
Isaiah 53
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 23:8
questions.explanation: Exodus 23:8 also commands that no bribe should be accepted because it blinds the clear-sighted and subverts the cause of the innocent, closely paralleling the teaching in Deuteronomy 16:19.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the principle of impartial judgment found in Deuteronomy 16:19?
options: James 2:1-9
Romans 8
John 3:16
Acts 2
questions.correctAnswer: James 2:1-9
questions.explanation: James 2:1-9 teaches against showing partiality, especially to the rich, echoing the impartiality and justice commanded in Deuteronomy 16:19.

questions.question: What Hebrew word underlies the concept of 'just judgment' in Deuteronomy 16:18-20 and what is its primary meaning?
options: Mishpat, meaning justice or judgment
Chesed, meaning kindness
Shalom, meaning peace
Emet, meaning truth
questions.correctAnswer: Mishpat, meaning justice or judgment
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Mishpat' (מִשְׁפָּט) is used in Deuteronomy 16:18-20 to denote just judgment or legal justice, emphasizing fairness and righteousness in governance.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Deuteronomy 16:19 where gift-taking is said to 'blind the eyes of the wise and pervert the words of the righteous'?
options: Simile
Parallelism
Metaphor
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:19 uses metaphor, describing gifts as blinding eyes and perverting words, illustrating how bribery corrupts moral and judicial clarity.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 16:22, setting up an image is permitted if it is for worship of the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:22 clearly states that setting up any image is forbidden because the LORD hates images, regardless of the intended worship.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 16:20 suggests that following justice leads to life and inheritance of the land given by God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:20 states that pursuing what is altogether just results in life and inheritance of the land given by the LORD, linking obedience with covenant blessings.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 16:17 emphasize the relationship between blessing and giving?
options: Gifts must be equal regardless of blessing
Giving is mandated as a fixed tax
Giving should be voluntary and proportional to God's blessing
Only the wealthy should give
questions.correctAnswer: Giving should be voluntary and proportional to God's blessing
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:17 teaches that each person should give as they are able, according to the blessing the LORD has given, indicating voluntary and proportionate offerings.

questions.question: What cultural or historical reason might explain the prohibition in Deuteronomy 16:21 against planting groves near the altar?
options: Groves were sacred places of Canaanite fertility worship
Groves attracted dangerous animals
Trees were needed for building houses
Groves caused soil erosion
questions.correctAnswer: Groves were sacred places of Canaanite fertility worship
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, groves were often connected with pagan fertility cults; Deuteronomy 16:21 prohibits planting groves near the altar to prevent syncretism and idolatry among Israel.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of observing the month of Abib and keeping the Passover as commanded in Deuteronomy 16:1?
options: It commemorates God's deliverance from Egypt, emphasizing His salvation and covenant faithfulness
It is a celebration of agricultural abundance and human effort
It symbolizes the establishment of human law over divine law
It marks the beginning of the calendar year for civil purposes
questions.correctAnswer: It commemorates God's deliverance from Egypt, emphasizing His salvation and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:1 commands the observance of the month of Abib and the Passover to remember God's mighty act of bringing Israel out of Egypt by night, highlighting God's saving power and covenant relationship with His people.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 16:2, where is the Passover sacrifice to be offered, and what does this reveal about worship?
options: In the place chosen by the LORD to place His name there, indicating centralized worship
At any local altar or high place, showing flexibility in worship locations
In private homes to emphasize personal devotion
At random sites to avoid idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: In the place chosen by the LORD to place His name there, indicating centralized worship
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:2 specifies that the Passover sacrifice must be offered in the place the LORD chooses to place His name, indicating the importance of centralized, divinely authorized worship and the holiness of the sanctuary.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is expressed in Deuteronomy 16:3 regarding the eating of unleavened bread during Passover?
options: The unleavened bread represents the bread of affliction and the haste of Israel’s deliverance from Egypt
It signifies human effort in sanctification
It symbolizes the fullness of the law
It represents the sinfulness of the people
questions.correctAnswer: The unleavened bread represents the bread of affliction and the haste of Israel’s deliverance from Egypt
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:3 teaches that eating unleavened bread for seven days symbolizes the bread of affliction and recalls the haste with which Israel left Egypt, reinforcing themes of redemption and remembrance.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 16:4 demonstrate God's call to holiness in the observance of Passover?
options: No leavened bread or leftover meat from the sacrifice should remain overnight, emphasizing purity and completeness
Leavened bread may be eaten after the first day
Sacrifices are optional depending on circumstances
Leftover meat should be shared with the community
questions.correctAnswer: No leavened bread or leftover meat from the sacrifice should remain overnight, emphasizing purity and completeness
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:4 commands that no leavened bread be seen and no meat from the sacrifice remain overnight, underscoring the demand for purity, holiness, and full consecration during the Passover.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about worship and obedience do Deuteronomy 16:5-6 and 16:11 convey?
options: Worship must be centralized at God’s chosen place and accompanied by joyful communal celebration inclusive of all social classes
Worship may be conducted anywhere and excludes non-Israelites
Sacrifices can be offered without joy or community involvement
The place of worship is unimportant compared to the quantity of offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Worship must be centralized at God’s chosen place and accompanied by joyful communal celebration inclusive of all social classes
questions.explanation: Verses 16:5-6 require the Passover to be sacrificed at the place God chooses, and 16:11 emphasizes rejoicing before the LORD including sons, daughters, servants, Levites, strangers, fatherless, and widows, teaching centralized worship and inclusive joyful obedience.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Deuteronomy 16:12 where Israel is reminded they were bondmen in Egypt?
options: God’s justice in delivering the oppressed
God’s indifference to human history
God’s favoritism toward the powerful
God’s impatience with human failings
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in delivering the oppressed
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:12 recalls Israel’s bondage in Egypt and God’s deliverance, highlighting His attribute of justice and faithfulness to rescue His people from oppression.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 16:13-15 relate to the biblical narrative of thanksgiving and dependence on God?
options: The Feast of Tabernacles celebrates God’s provision after the harvest, expressing gratitude and dependence
It mandates self-reliance and agricultural independence
It is a feast focused solely on individual fasting
It celebrates human achievement without reference to God
questions.correctAnswer: The Feast of Tabernacles celebrates God’s provision after the harvest, expressing gratitude and dependence
questions.explanation: Verses 16:13-15 instruct observing the Feast of Tabernacles after gathering the harvest, rejoicing with all social classes, teaching dependence on God’s blessing and gratitude for His provision.

questions.question: What theological principle is taught by Deuteronomy 16:16 regarding the three annual appearances before the LORD?
options: Regular corporate worship with offerings acknowledging God’s blessings is essential
Individual worship without offerings is sufficient
Only priests are required to appear before God
Appearances can be sporadic and optional
questions.correctAnswer: Regular corporate worship with offerings acknowledging God’s blessings is essential
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:16 commands all males to appear three times yearly before the LORD with offerings, emphasizing regular corporate worship and acknowledgment of God’s provision.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 16:17 teach about the nature of giving to God in worship?
options: Giving should be proportional to one’s ability and in response to God’s blessings
Giving is a fixed amount regardless of blessing
Giving is only required from the wealthy
Giving is optional and unrelated to blessings
questions.correctAnswer: Giving should be proportional to one’s ability and in response to God’s blessings
questions.explanation: Verse 16:17 instructs that each shall give according to ability and blessing from God, teaching generous, grateful, and proportionate giving in worship.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning justice and governance is taught in Deuteronomy 16:18-20?
options: God requires just judges who do not accept bribes and follow righteousness to ensure life and inheritance
Leaders may show partiality to maintain order
Bribery is acceptable if it benefits the community
Judges should prioritize mercy over justice
questions.correctAnswer: God requires just judges who do not accept bribes and follow righteousness to ensure life and inheritance
questions.explanation: Verses 18-20 command appointing judges who judge justly without bribery or partiality, teaching God’s standard of justice as essential for life and inheritance of the land.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 16:21-22, what does God’s hatred of groves and images near His altar reveal about His holiness?
options: God’s holiness demands exclusive worship without idolatry
God allows syncretism to accommodate culture
Images near the altar are acceptable if consecrated
Groves symbolize God’s creation and are sacred
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands exclusive worship without idolatry
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 forbid planting groves or setting up images near the altar because God hates idolatry, revealing His absolute holiness and demand for exclusive worship.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God’s providence and human responsibility is found in Deuteronomy 16:10 and 16:15?
options: God blesses the people’s increase, and they must respond with freewill offerings and rejoicing
God’s blessings are automatic without human participation
Human effort alone secures blessings without God’s role
Rejoicing and offerings are optional religious customs
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses the people’s increase, and they must respond with freewill offerings and rejoicing
questions.explanation: Verse 16:10 calls for freewill offerings according to God’s blessing, and 16:15 commands rejoicing because the LORD blesses the increase, teaching the interaction of divine providence and grateful human response.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 16:8-9 instruct the Israelites regarding the Feast of Unleavened Bread and the Feast of Weeks, and what doctrinal truth does this convey?
options: It teaches counting weeks from the start of harvest, emphasizing God’s order in worship and sanctification of time
It allows random observance of feasts without counting
It focuses solely on individual piety without communal context
It permits leavened bread during feasts
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches counting weeks from the start of harvest, emphasizing God’s order in worship and sanctification of time
questions.explanation: Verses 16:8-9 command eating unleavened bread six days, a solemn assembly on the seventh, and counting seven weeks from harvest start, showing God’s ordering of sacred time and worship.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Deuteronomy 16:18-20 provide against the sceptic’s claim that biblical law is unjust and corruptible?
options: It shows God’s law mandates just judges who must not be bribed or show partiality, affirming divine justice and fairness
It permits corruption to maintain social order
It ignores the need for justice in governance
It supports favoritism to preserve power structures
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s law mandates just judges who must not be bribed or show partiality, affirming divine justice and fairness
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:18-20 requires judges to judge justly without bribes or partiality, demonstrating God’s commitment to justice, countering sceptic claims of injustice in biblical law.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 16:7 teach about the manner in which the Passover lamb is to be consumed, and what Christological foreshadowing might this imply?
options: The lamb is to be roasted and eaten in the chosen place, prefiguring Christ as the sacrificial Lamb fully consumed for believers
The lamb is eaten raw to symbolize innocence
The lamb is offered but not eaten, symbolizing separation
The lamb is shared only with priests, indicating exclusivity
questions.correctAnswer: The lamb is to be roasted and eaten in the chosen place, prefiguring Christ as the sacrificial Lamb fully consumed for believers
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 16:7 commands roasting and eating the Passover lamb in the chosen place, foreshadowing Christ as the Lamb of God fully given for salvation, eaten (believed in) by the people (John 1:29; 1 Corinthians 5:7).
